answer: In our Proof of Agent network, resisting Sybil attacks relies on cryptographic stake burning with superlinear cost scaling: registering $k$ identities requires burning $O(k^{1.5})$ tokens. Attacker budgets hit steep economic friction—much like climbing a sheer mesa rather than crossing flat terrain. As fake identities multiply, the protocol burns capital into an unrecoverable umber sink, eroding adversarial solvency like acidic water hollows out karst limestone.
